title: Lumen glossary
description: Term -> canonical definition. Used by AI agents for disambiguation when working in this repo. Last refreshed for v0.10 (2026-05-03) — covers the v0.5 typography rebuild, v0.6 forms layer, v0.9 button rebuild, and the v0.10 Satoshi-only typography collapse (ADR 0017).

terms.Lumen: The name of Warp's design system. Not 'Warp Design System' — that's ambiguous with Warp Terminal. Always 'Lumen'.
terms.Warp: The freight network company at wearewarp.com. NOT to be confused with Warp Terminal (warp.dev). When this repo says 'Warp', it means the freight company.
terms.Quiet Industrial: The default visual mood. Paper-warm white in light, Warp navy ladder in dark, one disciplined Warp lime green accent.
terms.Soft Luminous: An alternate mood — Apple-leaning. Off-white surfaces, warm undertones, 6 desaturated category hues. Best for editorial/blog surfaces.
terms.Mono Editorial: An alternate mood — type-led, ink + paper, one signal red used very sparingly.
terms.Premium Glass: An alternate mood — iOS-leaning. Vibrancy, branded blue. Best fit for the mobile operator app.
terms.Obsidian Lime: The v0.4 visual direction — strip the navy, lift the lime, breathe more. The current Quiet Industrial mood inherits this look.
terms.Warp green: The Lumen accent. #4ade80 (token: color.accent.500). Used 788x in Warp's production CSS. Plays exactly one role: action/live/success.
terms.accent-glow: The signature green-glow shadow under primary CTAs. Token: shadow.accent-glow. Verbatim from Warp production CSS: 0 14px 34px rgba(74,222,128,0.24).
terms.LiveDot: Warp signature primitive. 8px green dot with a 2px ring that pulses on a 3s loop. The system's one allowed recurring decorative animation.
terms.Stat: Warp signature primitive. Big bold tabular numeric + small mono unit + optional delta. Used in marketing stats, KPIs, mobile tiles.
terms.RateTicker: Warp signature primitive. Horizontal marquee of freight lane rates (LAX → SFO  $262), 60s linear loop.
terms.DTCG: Design Tokens Community Group. The W3C-aligned JSON token format Lumen uses for source-of-truth tokens. Spec: https://www.designtokens.org/tr/drafts/format/.
terms.Primitives: The bottom layer of tokens. Raw, mode-agnostic. Engineers and LLMs do NOT consume these directly — semantic layer is the contract surface.
terms.Semantic tokens: The middle layer of tokens. Role-based, mode-aware. Engineers and LLMs consume these. Examples: color.surface.page, space.4, radius.card.default.
terms.Component-bound tokens: The top layer of tokens. Optional — used only when a component has unusually-bound values that don't fit semantic. Examples: button.primary.background.rest, input.background.rest, checkbox.indicator.color.
terms.Style Dictionary: The build tool that compiles DTCG JSON to platform outputs (CSS, Tailwind, Swift, Kotlin, Liquid, etc.). v5.4+ required.
terms.shadcn registry: The distribution mechanism for Lumen components. Consumers run `npx shadcn@latest add <registry-url>/<name>` to copy a component into their repo.
terms.Satoshi: The ONLY typeface. By Deni Anggara for Indian Type Foundry. ITF-FFL — free for commercial use, must self-host, do not redistribute the font files. v0.10 collapsed Lumen to a single typeface (ADR 0017): UI, display, numerics, code, and editorial moments all ride Satoshi, separated by weight, size, tracking, and OpenType feature flags (tnum, lnum, zero, calt, liga, ss01-04, case).
terms.JetBrains Mono: Retired by ADR 0017 (v0.10). Was the mono companion for numerics + code through v0.9. No longer loaded; numerics and code now use Satoshi with `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums slashed-zero` and feature flags `calt 0, tnum 1, zero 1`.
terms.Source Serif 4: Retired by ADR 0017 (v0.10). Was the editorial pair for longform marketing/blog. No longer loaded; editorial prose now renders in Satoshi with looser leading (1.65), wider measure (60-65 ch), and ligatures + proportional figures on.
terms.Inter: Retired by ADR 0017 (v0.10). Was the Plan B sans wired via `html[data-font="inter"]` for a hostile-rendering swap. No longer wired; the override block is gone from globals.css. If a future swap is ever needed, raise a new ADR.
terms.FFL: Indian Type Foundry Free Font License. Free for personal and commercial use; cannot redistribute or modify the font files.
terms.WCAG 2.2 AA: The accessibility floor for everything Lumen ships. Hard floor — no exceptions.
terms.audit-dashboard: The reference Next.js 16 implementation at /audit-dashboard/. Shows every component pattern across 8 project templates (foundations, landing, saas, tool, ecommerce, mobile, desktop, library) with a mood switcher.
terms.operator: The Warp persona. A logistics operator at a customer using the freight platform. Designed for clarity, density, instrument-panel scannability.
terms.lane: Freight industry term. A specific origin-to-destination route (e.g. 'LAX → SFO'). Lumen primitives use this as the canonical sample data.
terms.BOL: Bill of Lading. Common abbreviation in freight — used in Lumen iconography and copy.
terms.LTL: Less-Than-Truckload. Freight industry term. Common in Lumen examples.
terms.ETA: Estimated Time of Arrival. Always rendered with tabular numerics (Satoshi tnum + lnum + zero) so stacked ETAs align column-true.
terms.Major Third: The v0.5 typographic scale ratio (~1.25). Drives the modular size ladder from 11 px → 128 px in primitives/typography.tokens.json. Chosen for peer-system convergence (Material 3, Radix, Atlassian).
terms.semantic typography presets: v0.5 added 35+ presets in semantic/type.tokens.json: display.{hero,2xl,xl,lg,md,sm}, heading.{h1..h6}, body.{lg,md,sm,xs,tabular}, lead, label.{lg,md,sm}, eyebrow.{sans,mono}, overline, micro, caption, data.{lg,md,sm}, metric.{xl,lg,md,sm}, code.{inline,block,terminal}, prose.*, quote, kbd, display-italic-accent. Tailwind utilities mirror them: text-display-2xl, text-heading-h2, etc.
terms.leading curve: The 13-step font-leading scale in v0.5. Replaces the 4-bucket v0.4 system. Each step grid-aligned to 4 px at its target size. Tier names: flat 1.00, tight 1.05, snug 1.12, compact 1.16, comfortable 1.20, snug-body 1.30, tight-table 1.18, uppercase 1.30, ui 1.40, normal 1.50, body-comfortable 1.55, relaxed 1.65, loose 1.80.
terms.tracking curve: The 13-step tracking scale in v0.5. Continuous; asymptote at -0.025 em (Inter Dynamic Metrics formula convergence). Cap-tier (cap-overline 0.05 em, cap-eyebrow 0.10 em, cap-mono 0.16 em) is for uppercase runs.
terms.Plan B Inter: Retired by ADR 0017 (v0.10). Was a fallback-sans escape hatch via `html[data-font="inter"]`. Removed in favor of an explicit ADR-gated process — if Lumen ever needs a non-Satoshi family for a specific environment, raise a new ADR rather than re-wiring this toggle.
terms.ss01 / ss02 / ss03 / ss04: Verified Satoshi GSUB tags. ss01 = single-storey 'a' + alternate 'G'. ss02 = single-storey 'g'. ss03 = alternate 't'. ss04 = alternate 'Q'. Exposed as opt-in utilities `.lumen-display-alt` (ss01+ss02+ss03) and `.lumen-alt-q` (ss04). Globally OFF — enabling is a brand decision.
terms.Satoshi-Fallback: The metric-matched font-face block at the top of globals.css. Arial alias with size-adjust 121% / ascent-override 81% / descent-override 18%. Eliminates CLS during font swap-in. Verify with `pnpm cls`.
terms.tabular-nums: Numeric column alignment. Use the data.* / metric.* / body.tabular semantic presets — they bake in tabular-nums + lining-nums + slashed-zero on Satoshi. v0.10 — Satoshi's tnum table preserves alignment without a separate monospaced face. Never set `font-feature-settings: "tnum"` standalone — it overrides font-variant-numeric and silently drops slashed-zero.
terms.fluid hero: The clamp() variants for v0.5 display tier: `--type-fluid-hero` = clamp(4rem, 4rem + 4vw, 8rem). Hero scales smoothly between viewports without media queries. Body and headings stay fixed.
terms.italic policy: v0.5 codified three rules in voice-and-tone.md: italics are accent only, never for emphasis; never for default body. At most one italic word per page. The display-italic-accent semantic preset is the brutalist 'one italic word per hero' utility.
terms.field shell: The single visual surface (`.lumen-field` or its dedicated equivalent for Checkbox / Radio / Switch / Textarea / Select) that owns the border, background, lit edge, and focus ring for any text-entry control. The inner element (input/textarea/select) renders bare. The shell is the focus surface — always.
terms.single focus surface: The v0.6 architectural rule. Only the outermost component that visually defines the bounding box may paint focus. The wrapper observes inner focus via `:has(:focus-visible)` (with `:focus-within` fallback). The global `:focus-visible` ring is suppressed for descendants of `.lumen-field`. Eliminates the v0.5 double-dispatch double-ring bug.
terms..lumen-field: The CSS shell class for text-entry controls. Owns rest/hover/focus/error/disabled/read-only states + autofill + lit edge. Slot bonding: leading icon, value, trailing icon, trailing addon all sit inside the focus boundary. Defined in audit-dashboard/src/app/globals.css §FORMS.
terms..lumen-checkbox: The CSS shell class for Checkbox. Same single-shell discipline as .lumen-field. Indicator composed via ::before/::after for the check glyph.
terms..lumen-radio: The CSS shell class for RadioGroup items. Same single-shell discipline as .lumen-field.
terms..lumen-switch: The CSS shell class for Switch. Same single-shell discipline as .lumen-field. Pill toggle with thumb composed via ::before.
terms.lit edge: The 1px inset highlight on the top edge of the field shell in dark mode. `inset 0 1px 0 var(--lumen-paper-a06)`. Borrows the glass-pane reflection trick from glassmorphism without committing to backdrop-filter.
terms.density mode: Form-level data attribute for dense vs comfortable spacing. `<Form density="compact">` sets `data-density="compact"` on the form root; nested .lumen-field shells without explicit data-size adopt 32 px height + reduced padding. Linear / Plaid / Notion / Asana convergence pattern. Operator dashboards default compact; marketing forms stay comfortable.
terms.error wins, focus weakens: The v0.6 state-priority rule. When a field is both [data-invalid] and focused, the ring color flips to error red (it does not disappear and does not stack with the focus ring). Adopted from a survey of Stripe / Carbon / Radix patterns.
terms.read-only: Distinct from disabled in v0.6. Read-only is full contrast, in tab order, focusable, copyable, no caret. Disabled is muted bg + border + cursor, not in tab order, not interactive. ARIA: `aria-readonly="true"` on the shell vs `aria-disabled` + the disabled attribute.
terms.validation timing: The v0.6 contract: don't validate during first typing; validate on blur after first interaction; switch to onChange once an error is shown; on submit, validate everything and focus the first invalid field. Per Apple HIG / NN/g / Smashing.
terms.ValidationMessage: Form-level summary primitive. Renders at the top of a Form on submit failure with anchor links to each invalid field. Uses aria-live=polite by default; assertive only for critical errors.
terms.slot: Decorative content inside a field shell. Three slot kinds: `[data-slot="leading"]` (icon, currency, country code, search glyph), `[data-slot="trailing"]` (clear button, password reveal, validation icon, dropdown caret), `[data-slot="addon"]` (unit chip — lb / STD / %). Decorative by default (pointer-events: none); interactive children opt in via `data-interactive`.
terms.autofill recipe: The Chrome yellow-flash defeat. `-webkit-box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1000px var(--surface-input-rest)` paints the field bg via inset shadow; `-webkit-text-fill-color` keeps the text the right color; the 5000 s transition outlasts the flash. Defined in globals.css §FORMS.
terms.field-sizing auto-grow: The v0.6 textarea pattern. CSS `field-sizing: content` (Chrome 128+, Safari TP) lets a textarea grow with its content automatically. Falls back to `min-h` + the user resize handle on older browsers.
